analysis: What changed vs yesterday's briefs: the AI-spending verdict hardened from a split decision into a rout. Alphabet's -12.64% Thursday (worst day since its IPO) was only the first leg — Amazon and Intel reported after the close and both were sold on the same question, from opposite directions. Amazon paired its fastest AWS growth in nearly five years (+39% to $46.0B, record 13.9% operating margin) with a -$42.4B trailing free cash flow print and $77.3B of quarterly capex, and the market chose the cash line. Intel beat on the quarter (data-center/AI +78%) but guided Q4 well below consensus and warned the PC slump runs into 2027 with no positive free cash flow expected in the investment year — a demand warning, not a spending one, that still landed as -25% premarket and dragged AMD (-7% to -8%), Nvidia (-2.5% to -3%) and Broadcom (-4%) with it. Signal: guidance and cash conversion now outweigh beats — Reddit (-21.7% premarket) beat Q3 yet fell on a soft Q4 guide, and Pinterest missed outright. Noise: the selloff is not broad — Thursday's tape had 9 of 11 sectors up, advancers ahead on both exchanges, the Russell +1.01% and the equal-weight S&P +1.20% while the cap-weighted index fell 0.30%. The pain is concentrated in megacap tech and growth names, which is why Dow futures are near flat while Nasdaq futures are down over 2%. Carried forward: Fed hold at 3.75-4.00% with December-hike odds ~80-84%, Q3 GDP 3.4%, core PCE 3.1% y/y — today's 8:30 a.m. ET Employment Cost Index feeds that same hike pricing, and Exxon/Chevron before the bell test whether energy can keep offsetting tech.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a tech-led soft open: Nasdaq 100 futures -2.19%, S&P 500 futures -0.97%, Dow futures +0.05% as of 5:36 a.m. ET, as Amazon and Intel earnings extend Thursday's tech selloff into Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A concentrated tech open, not broad risk-off — the Dow near flat shows the pressure is in megacap tech and chips, not the whole market.

headlines.headline: Amazon falls ~7% premarket (to ~$227.42 per Finnhub's 06:53 ET read, vs $243.79 close) after Q3 missed: net sales $201.9B vs ~$202.31B expected, EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.96 expected, despite AWS +39% to $46.0B (fastest in nearly five years) and a record 13.9% operating margin. Trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to -$42.4B from +$14.8B a year earlier on $77.3B of quarterly property/equipment spending; 2026 cash capex held at ~$220B, with Jassy projecting AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Q4 sales guide of $240-247B has a midpoint below consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a record margin and accelerating AWS could not offset the cash line — the market is grading AI spenders on free cash flow, and Amazon just joined Alphabet on the wrong side of that test.

headlines.headline: Intel plunges ~25% premarket despite a Q3 beat: revenue $16.5B (+21% y/y), adjusted EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.41 expected, data-center/AI +78% to $7.3B and foundry +58% to $6.7B — but Q4 guidance of $15-16B revenue and $0.25 EPS trails the ~$17.1B / $0.43 consensus, client computing fell 5% to $8.1B, and the company warned the PC market declines into at least H1 2027 (about -10% next year) with an Israel fab disruption costing ~$300M per quarter and no positive free cash flow expected in the 2027 investment year.
headlines.why_it_matters: A demand warning from Intel hits the whole chip complex — Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom are all down premarket in sympathy, so this is a sector read, not just one stock.

headlines.headline: Alphabet steadies after Thursday's rout: GOOGL fell 12.64% Thursday to $283.82, its worst day since its 2004 IPO, on the Q3 miss (revenue $127.58B, EPS $2.12) and -$9.07B free cash flow; premarket Friday it is only -0.42% to $282.63 (Finnhub, 06:53 ET).
headlines.why_it_matters: The bleeding has paused, not reversed — Alphabet is no longer the day's driver, but its Thursday repricing set the bar Amazon and Intel then failed.

headlines.headline: Megacap premarket snapshot (Finnhub, ~06:53 ET): Microsoft -0.66% to $526.63, Nvidia -2.95% to $207.35, Meta -1.52% to $615.03, Apple -1.09% to $345.11, Tesla -2.28% to $394.12 — all lower, with chips leading the declines.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even Thursday's winners are being pulled in — Microsoft's cash-backed beat is no longer an offset when the whole tech complex is de-risking into the open.

headlines.headline: After-hours selloff spread beyond the megacaps: Reddit -21.69% premarket to $101.49 (Finnhub) after beating Q3 ($1.40 EPS on $895M revenue) but guiding Q4 revenue of $1.00-1.03B vs ~$1.05B consensus; Pinterest fell ~12% after missing Q3 ($0.46 vs $0.49 expected, revenue $1.17B vs ~$1.21B); Roblox and Twilio also fell sharply after hours on soft guidance.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance is punishing growth names across the board — beats are being sold when the outlook softens, which widens the open's drag beyond the index heavyweights.

headlines.headline: Prior session (Thu Oct 29) hid a rotation: S&P 500 -0.30% to 7,720.39, Nasdaq -1.38% to 26,184.72, Dow -0.25% to 52,342.56 — but 9 of 11 sectors rose, advancers outnumbered decliners on both exchanges, the Russell 2000 gained 1.01% to 2,859.22, and the equal-weight S&P rose 1.20% while the cap-weighted index fell. 10-year yield ended near 4.98%, WTI near $103.37, gold near $4,004, bitcoin near $78,134.
headlines.why_it_matters: The headline declines overstate the damage — breadth held up Thursday, so today's question is whether the Amazon/Intel leg finally breaks that rotation or stays contained in tech.

headlines.headline: Oil rebounds premarket (WTI +1.49% to ~$103.52, Brent +1.58% to ~$116.70 per TipRanks) ahead of ExxonMobil and Chevron earnings before the bell; Fed speakers Daly (San Francisco) and Musalem (St. Louis) also speak today.
headlines.why_it_matters: Energy is the morning's offset candidate — strong oil-major prints would reinforce the rotation out of tech, while soft ones would remove the tape's main cushion.
